claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a closely matched derivative has high saturation magnetization.
The baseline single-phase fcc FeCoNi or matched derivative has a coercive field at or below 100 Oe at room temperature.
Adding 1–5 at.% carbon can preserve the single-phase fcc structure of FeCoNi under suitable processing conditions.
Added carbon occupies interstitial sites in the fcc FeCoNi lattice.
Interstitial carbon produces localized lattice distortions in fcc FeCoNi.
Interstitial carbon increases the defect density in fcc FeCoNi.
The local strain fields produced by interstitial carbon enhance the magnetocrystalline anisotropy of the alloy.
Carbon-induced lattice distortions and defects act as pinning sites for magnetic domain walls.
Enhanced magnetocrystalline anisotropy causes more effective domain-wall pinning.
More effective domain-wall pinning increases the applied magnetic field required for magnetization reversal.
Adding 1–5 at.% carbon while retaining a single fcc phase will increase coercivity significantly relative to an undoped matched baseline.
The carbon-modified alloy will have a room-temperature coercive field greater than 100 Oe.
The carbon-modified alloy will retain high saturation magnetization.

contradictions.description: The boundary declares samples containing secondary carbides outside the hypothesis's intended domain, whereas the falsification rule treats carbide formation as falsification of the hypothesis rather than as a failed intervention or an excluded sample.
